newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil monetary base expands 2.4 pct in Sept.
newsitem.headline: Brazil monetary base expands 2.4 pct in Sept.

text.p: Brazil's monetary base as measured by daily averages expanded 2.4 percent in the month of September, the Central Bank said.

In a statement, the bank also said Brazil's net public sector debt stood at 252.7 billion reais, equivalent to 35.0 percent of gross domestic product. Of that total, internal debt accounted for 221.1 billion reais and the remaining 31.6 billion reais was foreign debt.
Brazil's operational deficit in the year to August was equivalent to 3.88 percent of GDP, up from 3.70 percent in July.

The Central Bank said that of the 3.88 percent operational deficit, the federal government and the Central Bank accounted for 1.41 percent, state and municipal governments, 2.19 percent and state companies, 0.29 percent.
The Central Bank said the monetary base grew 14.8 percent from September 1995 through September 1996, up from 12.5 percent in the August 1995-1996 period.

Brazil's public sector borrowing requirement, encompassing federal, state and municipal governments, the Central Bank and state companies showed a deficit of 6.36 percent of GDP in the January through August 1996 period.
